When the Abernethys decided to adopt a child, Agatha voiced her disapproval and misgivings. Nell later offered a dramatic apology at Agatha's home, which Agatha accepted graciously. Over the subsequent years, Agatha observed Nell's development, eventually admitting she had been wrong about her. Following Obed Abernethy's sudden death, Agatha assisted the family, checking his pulse and spending the night at Grey Shutters to support Thirza and Nell.

Following Obed Abernethy's sudden death, Agatha assisted the family, checking his pulse and spending the night at Grey Shutters to support Thirza and Nell.

label: History
value: Flossie cheated during a spelling exercise at Brierley school.
unit: While attending Brierley school, Flossie cheated during a spelling exercise and was caught by Nell Harcourt, causing her to misspell the word. During an outdoor gathering, she walked a wooden fence with ease to prove her skill and then challenged Nell to walk the ridgepole of Mr. Pembroke's kitchen roof; when Nell fell and was injured, Flossie suffered intense distress and guilt over the potential outcome. She later visited Nell while she was recovering from her fractured ankle. During preparation for a school concert, Flossie became moody when she was denied the role of the fairy queen due to her weight, though she later attended the event and acknowledged Nell's stellar performance. She won top prize for knitted lace at a local fair. Joining the Regent's class, she prepared for the Entrance exam, though she struggled with arithmetic. After taking the exam, she barely passed by a three-point margin. Flossie then attended Regent's Academy in town, boarding at the same house as Frank Stockley, and decided to return for another year of study after finishing her first.

label: History
value: Hugh spent three years in Alberta.
unit: After spending three years in Alberta due to his father's health, Hugh returned home and entered Brierley school. On his first day back, he teased Nell Harcourt by pulling her braid and calling her 'carrots', leading her to smash her slate over his head. Though Hugh stood up to take the blame for the incident and apologized afterward, Nell refused to forgive him. Over the following terms, Hugh maintained an intense academic competition with Nell while continuing to excel in recitations at community concerts. During a lily-maid play gone wrong on the pond, Hugh rescued Nell in his dory and again sought her friendship, but was met with cold rejection, leading him to ignore her socially while intensifying their academic rivalry. Entering the Regent's class in Port Marlow, Hugh took the Second Year course to obtain a First Class teacher's license in one year, eventually winning the prestigious Medal. Upon learning that Nell needed to stay in Brierley to care for Thirza and wished to teach at the local school, Hugh generously withdrew his own application for the Brierley position and accepted a teaching role in Pale Sands instead. Meeting Nell on the road shortly after, he accepted her gratitude and forgiveness, establishing a warm friendship with her at last.

value: Isolde Pembroke returns home to Pear Hill.
unit: Isolde Pembroke returns home to Pear Hill after visiting her aunt in Delford and soon meets Nell Harcourt, who visits with Thirza Abernethy. The two girls quickly become bosom friends, swearing a solemn vow over a pretend stream to remain loyal friends forever. Together they share books, play around Pear Hill and the surrounding woods, and create a playhouse named Larkrise. After consuming three glassfuls of home-brewed cordial at Grey Shutters, Isolde becomes dizzy, giggles, falls asleep, and develops a severe headache. Her mother assumes Nell deliberately got Isolde drunk and forbids Isolde from playing or speaking with Nell. Isolde secretly meets Nell near the Nymph's Well to bid her a tearful farewell, giving her a lock of her hair, and later sends her a note and a tissue-paper bookmark at school. After Nell saves Isolde's younger sister Posy Fay from croup, Mrs. Pembroke realizes her mistake and restores their friendship. Isolde attends a concert with Nell and hosts her great-aunt Lavinia Pembroke, who funds Isolde's music lessons after Nell intercedes on her behalf. Over the years, Isolde and Nell attend Brierley school together, craft stories for a writing club, and travel to town for a fair with her father and Miss Lavinia Pembroke. When Nell attends Regent's class while Isolde does not, and later when Nell goes away to the Academy, the two remain loyal companions.

label: History
value: Nell was born in Nova Scotia.
unit: Born in Nova Scotia to Edmund and Bertha Harcourt, Nell spent part of her early childhood in an asylum before being taken in by Thirza Abernethy and Obed at Grey Shutters. Though initially taken by mistake instead of a boy, she quickly bonded with Obed and Thirza despite several humorous clashes over her vibrant imagination, wild temper, and impulsive antics. On her first day of school in Brierley, she reacted furiously when classmate Hugh Carrow pulled her hair and called her 'Carrots,' smashing her slate over his head and initiating a bitter five-year feud and academic rivalry. Over the years, Nell formed a deep friendship with Isolde Pembroke, earned top marks in school, and excelled in dramatic recitations. After attempting to dye her hair black and accidentally turning it green, she was forced to cut it off, though it later grew back into a dark auburn. After completing school at Brierley, she attended the Academy at Regent's, where she won the prestigious Avery scholarship. However, upon discovering Thirza's failing eyesight and financial hardship, Nell selflessly gave up her university plans to stay home, taking up a teaching position in Brierley and finally reconciling with Hugh Carrow.

label: History
value: Obed Abernethy lived as a quiet farmer
unit: Obed Abernethy lived as a quiet farmer at Grey Shutters in Brierley with his sister Thirza. Facing increasing difficulty finding farm labor and dealing with a heart condition, he and Thirza arranged to adopt an orphan boy. When Obed went to the station at Alder River, he discovered that a mistake had brought an eleven-year-old girl, Nell Harcourt, instead. Unable to bring himself to turn her away, Obed brought her home and gently persuaded Thirza to keep her. Over the next three years, Obed formed a deep, affectionate bond with Nell, delighting in her chatter, supporting her school accomplishments, and occasionally buying her special gifts like a stylish Christmas dress. As his heart trouble worsened, he was advised by a doctor to avoid strenuous labor and excitement. Shortly after Nell won the Avery scholarship, Obed suffered a fatal heart attack and passed away peacefully at home.

unit: Obed Abernethy lived as a quiet farmer at Grey Shutters in Brierley with his sister Thirza. Facing increasing difficulty finding farm labor and dealing with a heart condition, he and Thirza arranged to adopt an orphan boy. When Obed went to the station at Alder River, he discovered that a mistake had brought an eleven-year-old girl, Nell Harcourt, instead. Unable to bring himself to turn her away, Obed brought her home and gently persuaded Thirza to keep her. Over the next three years, Obed formed a deep, affectionate bond with Nell, delighting in her chatter, supporting her school accomplishments, and occasionally buying her special gifts like a stylish Christmas dress. As his heart trouble worsened, he was advised by a doctor to avoid strenuous labor and excitement. Shortly after Nell won the Avery scholarship, Obed suffered a fatal heart attack and passed away peacefully at home.

label: History
value: Odette grew up in Brierley.
unit: Odette grew up in Brierley as the daughter of Gorham Pullen and Mrs. Alexander Tranter. While attending the local school under Mr. Pidgeon, she participated in childhood games, theatrical dialogues, and a girls' tale-writing club, while also nearly drowning during a boat outing on the Lake of Glassy Waters before her father saved her. She took part in playing the lily maid Elaine with Nell Harcourt, Isolde Pembroke, and Opal Pettigrew, but panicked when Nell drifted out of sight on a flat boat. Upon entering the Regent's Entrance preparation class taught by Miss Thorne, she resolved to become a teacher to earn an independent living. She successfully passed the Entrance examinations and subsequently attended Regent's Academy, earning high marks in domestic science and passing her final tests with steady composure. Following her qualification, she accepted a position from the Stonebridge trustees to teach at their school.

value: Mr. Pidgeon served as the schoolmaster at Brierley school.
unit: Mr. Pidgeon served as the schoolmaster at Brierley school. label: History
value: Miss Agnes Thorne was hired as the new teacher for Brierley school.
unit: Miss Agnes Thorne was hired as the new teacher for Brierley school, becoming the first female educator employed there. She introduced various innovative activities for her students, including physical culture exercises, bi-weekly recitation Friday afternoons, and field trips to the forest to study nature. In November, she proposed that the school organize a performance on Christmas Night to raise funds for a schoolhouse flag. She later established an after-school group to provide extra instruction for pupils preparing for the Regent's entrance exam. Although she received an offer to teach at a grade school in her home district, her strong interest in her Brierley pupils led her to stay for another year and guide them through their Entrance examinations. At the end of that final school term, she parted ways with her students upon completing her tenure at Brierley.
